```{r}
#| label: setup
# Load cfbstats from the checkout when the package is not installed, so the
# site build does not require a package install (decision 0030).
if (requireNamespace("cfbstats", quietly = TRUE)) {

} else {

  }
  for (src in sort(list.files(

}
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)

library(ggiraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
# altdoc renders in a temp dir; point the knit wd at the project root so
# data/*.parquet and tar_read() resolve (CFBSTATS_ROOT is set in the site build).
root <- cfbstats_root()
if (nzchar(root)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
}

set_girafe_defaults(
  opts_hover = opts_hover(
    css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);"
  ),
  opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"),
  opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip(

  ),
  opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5),
  opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"),
  opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
)

# Wilson interval for a binomial proportion.
wilson <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) {
  p <- x / n
  d <- 1 + z^2 / n
  c <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / d
  h <- (z / d) * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  c(lo = pmax(0, c - h), hi = pmin(1, c + h))
}
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-24. Draft classes
after the last complete draft are right-censored and carry no outcomes, so
they are excluded from every rate below rather than counted as failures.
Each season's position comes from the roster table, joined by athlete id
and season.*
:::

## 1. Introduction

The previous post measured how often eligible college seasons end in an NFL
outcome, over the whole population at once. But nobody watches football that
way. The draft broadcasts positional differences every spring:
quarterbacks and pass rushers go early, punters appear once, late, on a
conference call. Position is also the first thing any draft model would
condition on, so the rates need tabulating where they actually vary.

This post splits those eligible player-seasons by the position the player
lined up at in that season, and asks five questions:

+ *Expecting quarterbacks to be the most draftable position*
+ *Expecting first-round picks to concentrate among quarterbacks*
+ *Expecting quarterbacks to be picked earliest on average, in every draft class*
+ *Expecting the per-season chance of NFL entry to rise with waiting, for every position*
+ *Expecting quarterbacks to arrive through the draft while other positions lean on the undrafted route*

Each question is a claim the data can settle, answered with a table or
figure backed by an assertion.

## 2. Data and terms

The unit is the same as before: a **player-season**, one player's college
season with a recorded stat line. Rates are computed over
**eligible player-seasons**, seasons whose following draft the player could
have been selected in. Draft classes whose outcomes may occur in the future
are excluded rather than counted as misses.

Each season carries the roster position the player was listed at that
season; a few carry none and form their own group in Table 1. Roster
listings use two dozen shorthand codes, from QB to LS, and neighboring
codes describe the same professional role. The analysis groups them into
nine reader-facing groups, plus a tenth row for the seasons with none
recorded.

```{r}
#| label: group-terms
group_terms <- tribble(
  ~Group                  , ~"Roster codes in the group"                                                                                                                                  ,
  "Quarterback"           , "QB"                                                                                                                                                          ,
  "Running back"          , "RB, FB"                                                                                                                                                      ,
  "Receiver"              , "WR"                                                                                                                                                          ,
  "Tight end"             , "TE"                                                                                                                                                          ,
  "Offensive line"        , "T, G, C, OL"                                                                                                                                                 ,
  "Defensive line"        , "DL, DE, DT, NT, EDGE"                                                                                                                                        ,
  "Linebacker"            , "LB, ILB, OLB"                                                                                                                                                ,
  "Defensive back"        , "DB, S, CB"                                                                                                                                                   ,
  "Special teams"         , "PK, P, LS, PR"                                                                                                                                               ,
  "Position not recorded" , "Seasons whose roster entry carries no usable position code, including the rare ATH listing (concentrated in earlier draft classes), or no roster row at all"
)
kable(group_terms, caption = "Table 1: the position groups used throughout")
```

A note on the uncertainty intervals: whenever a percentage is reported
below, it comes with a 95 percent confidence interval, the range the true
rate plausibly occupies given how many seasons were observed. The style is
Wilson's, chosen because it behaves well for rare events like these.

```{r}
#| label: load
# The connection message is an implementation detail; the reader sees only
# the counts in the visible chunks.
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfbstats.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
outcomes <- tbl(con, "outcomes") |> collect()
roster_pos <- tbl(con, "roster") |>
  # A few players carry two roster rows in one season (mid-season moves);
  # they always agree on the position, so one row per player-season is kept.
  select(playerId, season, position) |>
  distinct() |>
  collect()
dbDisconnect(con)

risk <- outcomes |>
  filter(draft_eligible, outcome_observed_d) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(outcome_drafted_d, outcome_signed_udfa_d, outcome_nfl_entry_d),
      ~ coalesce(.x, FALSE)
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(roster_pos, by = c("playerId", "season"))

pos_group <- c(
  QB = "Quarterback",
  RB = "Running back",
  FB = "Running back",
  WR = "Receiver",
  TE = "Tight end",
  T = "Offensive line",
  G = "Offensive line",
  C = "Offensive line",
  OL = "Offensive line",
  DL = "Defensive line",
  DE = "Defensive line",
  DT = "Defensive line",
  NT = "Defensive line",
  EDGE = "Defensive line",
  LB = "Linebacker",
  ILB = "Linebacker",
  OLB = "Linebacker",
  DB = "Defensive back",
  S = "Defensive back",
  CB = "Defensive back",
  PK = "Special teams",
  P = "Special teams",
  LS = "Special teams",
  PR = "Special teams"
)
n_risk_pre <- nrow(risk)
risk <- risk |>
  mutate(
    group = dplyr::coalesce(
      dplyr::recode(position, !!!pos_group, .default = "Position not recorded"),
      "Position not recorded"
    )
  )

n_risk <- nrow(risk)
n_players <- n_distinct(risk$playerId)
```

```{r}
#| label: risk-set
risk_set <- tibble(
  Measure = c("Eligible player-seasons", "Distinct players"),
  Count = format(c(n_risk, n_players), big.mark = ",")
)
kable(risk_set, caption = "Table 2: the risk set")
```

```{r}
#| label: grain-guard
#| include: false
# The guarded position join adds or drops no rows, and the outcome labels
# stay mutually exclusive after the join.
stopifnot(
  nrow(risk) == n_risk_pre,
  !any(is.na(risk$group)),
  !any(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d),
  all(
    risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d ==
      (risk$outcome_drafted_d | risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d)
  )
)
```

Players move, and a player can carry a different code in a different
season; each season is counted at the position it was played at.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 How often each position is drafted

*Expecting quarterbacks to be the most draftable position.* ❌ **The
expectation does not hold.** The quarterback row sits mid-table; the top
belongs to the offensive line, the bottom to the specialists.

```{r}
#| label: rates
rates <- risk |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    seasons = n(),
    players = n_distinct(playerId),
    drafted_ev = sum(outcome_drafted_d),
    entry_ev = sum(outcome_nfl_entry_d),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    drafted = drafted_ev / seasons,
    entry = entry_ev / seasons,
    drafted_lo = 100 * wilson(drafted_ev, seasons)["lo"],
    drafted_hi = 100 * wilson(drafted_ev, seasons)["hi"]
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(drafted))

rates_out <- rates |>
  transmute(
    `Position group` = group,
    `Eligible seasons` = format(seasons, big.mark = ","),
    `Players` = format(players, big.mark = ","),
    `Drafted` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * drafted),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f%%, %.1f%%]", drafted_lo, drafted_hi),
    `NFL entry` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * entry)
  )
kable(
  rates_out,
  caption = "Table 3: drafted and NFL-entry prevalence by position group"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: rates-bars
bars <- rates |>
  select(group, drafted, entry) |>
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "outcome", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(
    outcome = dplyr::recode(outcome, drafted = "Drafted", entry = "NFL entry"),
    group = factor(group, levels = rev(rates$group))
  )

p_rates <- ggplot(bars, aes(p, group, fill = outcome)) +
  geom_col_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = paste0(
        group,
        ", ",
        tolower(outcome),
        ": ",
        scales::percent(p, accuracy = 0.1)
      )
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .05))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Drafted" = "#1B9E77", "NFL entry" = "gray55")) +
  theme_cfbstats() +
  labs(
    x = "Prevalence among eligible player-seasons",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  )
girafe(ggobj = p_rates, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 6)
```

```{r}
#| label: rates-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  # The draft event stays rare inside every position group.
  all(rates$drafted < 0.10),
  # The claimed ordering: offensive line on top, special teams at the bottom,
  # quarterbacks mid-pack.
  rates$group[1] == "Offensive line",
  rates$drafted[rates$group == "Offensive line"] >
    rates$drafted[rates$group == "Quarterback"],
  rates$drafted[rates$group == "Quarterback"] >
    rates$drafted[rates$group == "Special teams"]
)
```

Out of every 100 eligible offensive-line seasons, about 8 end with the
player drafted and 16 with the player reaching the NFL by any route,
against 4 and 7 for quarterbacks and 1 and 4 for specialists. The drafted
spread from top to bottom is more than sixfold. The offensive-line result
deserves a qualifier that Section 5 returns to: linemen rarely record a
statistic, and this population counts only seasons with a stat line, so
the 8.2 percent is the draft rate of the small, selected minority of
linemen who left one.

### 3.2 Where the first round goes

*Expecting first-round picks to concentrate among quarterbacks.* ✅ **The
expectation holds.** The recurring cast of this series is, as it happens,
all quarterbacks: Joe Burrow first overall in 2020, Cameron Ward first
overall in 2025, Jordan Travis in the fifth round in 2024, and Shane
Buechele and Kyle Allen undrafted. The cast's one-position makeup is itself
a hint at the shape of the first round.

```{r}
#| label: round-mix
round_mix <- risk |>
  filter(outcome_drafted_d) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    drafted_seasons = n(),
    round1 = sum(outcome_draft_round_d == 1L),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(round1_share = round1 / drafted_seasons) |>
  arrange(desc(round1_share))

round_out <- round_mix |>
  transmute(
    `Position group` = group,
    `Drafted seasons` = format(drafted_seasons, big.mark = ","),
    `Of which round 1` = round1,
    `Round-1 share` = scales::percent(round1_share, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
kable(
  round_out,
  caption = "Table 4: the round-1 share of drafted seasons by position group"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: round-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  round_mix$group[1] == "Quarterback",
  round_mix$round1_share[1] > 0.25,
  round_mix$round1_share[1] >
    2 * round_mix$round1_share[round_mix$group == "Running back"],
  # The cast's pinned facts.
  risk$outcome_draft_pick_d[
    risk$player == "Joe Burrow" & risk$outcome_drafted_d
  ] ==
    1L,
  risk$outcome_draft_pick_d[
    risk$player == "Cameron Ward" & risk$outcome_drafted_d
  ] ==
    1L,
  risk$outcome_draft_round_d[
    risk$player == "Jordan Travis" & risk$outcome_drafted_d
  ] ==
    5L,
  all(risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d[
    risk$player %in%
      c("Shane Buechele", "Kyle Allen") &
      risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d
  ])
)
```

When a quarterback does get drafted, the pick is a first-rounder 26.2
percent of the time, well ahead of the 16.8 percent of defensive linemen,
the next group. The draft's most valuable resource, the early pick, is
spent on one position disproportionately, while the back of the draft is
where the running backs and specialists hear their names. A quarterback
season is average in its chance of any pick and extreme in what that pick
is worth. Both facts matter for modeling: the drafted label treats
Burrow's first pick and Travis's 171st as the same event, and the position
term is where a model can recover part of the difference.

### 3.3 Where in the draft each position lands, over the years

*Expecting quarterbacks to be picked earliest on average, in every draft
class.* ❌ **The expectation does not hold.** The measure is the average
overall pick among each group's drafted seasons, across draft classes. Over
the whole span quarterbacks do carry the lowest average, pick 112, with
defensive linemen at 114 and specialists far back at 179. But the
year-to-year ordering is noisy: quarterbacks are the lowest group in only
5 of the 14 draft classes.

```{r}
#| label: pick-trend
pick_trend <- risk |>
  filter(outcome_drafted_d, !is.na(outcome_draft_pick_d)) |>
  group_by(group, draft_year) |>
  summarise(
    picks = n(),
    avg_pick = mean(outcome_draft_pick_d),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(picks >= 5)

p_pick <- ggplot(
  pick_trend,
  aes(draft_year, avg_pick, color = group)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 126.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray70") +
  geom_line_interactive(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = paste0(
        group,
        ", ",
        draft_year,
        ": pick ",
        sprintf("%.0f", avg_pick),
        " on average (",
        picks,
        " picks)"
      )
    ),
    size = 2.6
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2012, 2025, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  theme_cfbstats() +
  labs(
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Average overall pick among drafted seasons",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Group-year cells with fewer than 5 picks omitted. Dashed line: average across all drafted seasons."
  )
girafe(ggobj = p_pick, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5.5)
```

```{r}
#| label: pick-guard
#| include: false
qb_avg_all <- mean(pick_trend$avg_pick[pick_trend$group == "Quarterback"])
complete_groups <- pick_trend |>
  count(group) |>
  filter(n == max(n)) |>
  pull(group)
group_means <- pick_trend |>
  filter(group %in% complete_groups) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(m = mean(avg_pick), .groups = "drop")
lowest_per_year <- pick_trend |>
  group_by(draft_year) |>
  slice_min(avg_pick, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
stopifnot(
  # Quarterbacks carry the lowest long-run average pick among the groups
  # with a published cell in every draft class.
  group_means$group[which.min(group_means$m)] == "Quarterback",
  qb_avg_all < 120,
  # But not in every class: the yearly minimum changes hands.
  sum(lowest_per_year$group == "Quarterback") == 5,
  sum(lowest_per_year$group == "Quarterback") < nrow(lowest_per_year),
  # The dashed reference line in the figure is the pooled average pick.
  abs(
    mean(risk$outcome_draft_pick_d[
      risk$outcome_drafted_d & !is.na(risk$outcome_draft_pick_d)
    ]) -
      126.6
  ) <
    0.05
)
```

The instability has a mundane source: a class hands each position only a
handful of picks, so one early selection moves a group's average by dozens
of slots. The offensive line's cell appears only from 2018 on, the
stat-line selection of Section 3.1 again, and swings from pick 58 to pick
170 on a dozen picks' worth of evidence. What survives year to year is the
ordering at the extremes: quarterbacks and defensive linemen live in the
first two rounds on average, running backs and specialists in the back
half.

### 3.4 The per-season chance of entry, by position

*Expecting the chance of NFL entry to rise with waiting, for every
position.* ❌ **The expectation does not hold, for one group.** The measure
is again the discrete-time hazard: among players still unentered after 1, 2, 3, ... eligible seasons,
the share whose very next draft is the one that takes them. Every group with at least three published
indices climbs over its first three; the offensive line publishes only two,
and climbs over both. Special teams climbs to its third eligible season,
then falls back.

```{r}
#| label: hazard
hazard <- risk |>
  group_by(group, eligible_season_index) |>
  summarise(
    seasons = n(),
    entry = mean(outcome_nfl_entry_d),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(seasons >= 50)

hazard_wide <- hazard |>
  select(group, eligible_season_index, entry) |>
  mutate(entry = scales::percent(entry, accuracy = 0.1)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = eligible_season_index,
    values_from = entry,
    names_prefix = "Season "
  )
kable(
  hazard_wide,
  caption = "Table 5: the per-season hazard of NFL entry by position group and eligible season index (indices with fewer than 50 seasons omitted)"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: hazard-guard
#| include: false
entry_by <- function(g) {
  hazard$entry[hazard$group == g][order(hazard$eligible_season_index[
    hazard$group == g
  ])]
}
# Groups with at least three published indices all rise over their first three;
# the offensive line only publishes two.
multi <- unique(hazard$group)[
  vapply(
    unique(hazard$group),
    function(g) length(entry_by(g)) >= 3L,
    logical(1)
  )
]
stopifnot(
  all(
    vapply(
      setdiff(multi, "Special teams"),
      function(g) all(diff(entry_by(g)[1:3]) > 0),
      logical(1)
    )
  ),
  # The one exception: special teams falls back at index 4.
  entry_by("Special teams")[4] < entry_by("Special teams")[3]
)
```

The climb is steep everywhere it happens. Quarterbacks go from 2.6 percent
in their first eligible season to 25.2 percent at their fourth; tight ends
reach 26.8 and 28.3 percent at their third and fourth seasons, the highest
hazard in the table. The special-teams exception fits how that group is
built: kickers and punters still unentered after three eligible seasons are
increasingly the ones nobody was planning to draft, and the marginal fourth
season does not change that. For the skill positions, an additional
eligible season reads as accumulated proof, and the draft chance rises with
it.

### 3.5 How each position reaches the NFL

*Expecting quarterbacks to arrive through the draft while other positions
lean on the undrafted route.* ✅ **The expectation holds.** Conditioning on
the seasons that end in NFL entry, the undrafted share varies by position, and the ordering matches the
fan's model of the sport.

```{r}
#| label: udfa-share
udfa_share <- risk |>
  filter(outcome_nfl_entry_d) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    entrants = n(),
    udfa = sum(outcome_signed_udfa_d),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(share = udfa / entrants) |>
  arrange(desc(share))

udfa_out <- udfa_share |>
  transmute(
    `Position group` = group,
    `Entrants` = format(entrants, big.mark = ","),
    `Arrived as UDFA` = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
kable(
  udfa_out,
  caption = "Table 6: the undrafted share of NFL entrants by position group"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: udfa-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  udfa_share$group[1] == "Special teams",
  udfa_share$group[nrow(udfa_share)] == "Quarterback",
  min(udfa_share$share) < 0.5,
  max(udfa_share$share) > 0.65
)
```

Among positions with real sample sizes, quarterbacks are the only group
where the draft is the majority route: 43.5 percent of quarterback entrants
arrived undrafted, against 61.4 percent for receivers and 68.6 percent for
specialists. The overall figure from the previous post, 56.6 percent, sits
between the extremes, and the position split explains part of why the
aggregate looks the way it does. Buechele and Allen, the cast's two UDFA
members, are both quarterbacks who entered through the minority route of
their majority-drafted position.

## 4. Summary

+ The drafted rate spans from 8.2 percent of eligible offensive-line seasons
  down to 1.2 percent for special teams, a more than sixfold spread;
  quarterbacks sit mid-table at 3.7 percent.
+ Quarterbacks dominate the top of the draft: 26.2 percent of drafted
  quarterback seasons are first-round picks, well ahead of any other
  position's share.
+ Quarterbacks carry the lowest long-run average pick (112) among the
  groups with a cell in every draft class, but they are the year's lowest
  group in only 5 of 14 classes.
+ The per-season hazard of entry rises steeply with waiting for every group
  that publishes at least three indices; special teams peaks at eligible
  season three and falls back at season four.
+ Quarterbacks are the only position group whose entrants mostly arrive
  drafted (56.5 percent); for specialists the undrafted route carries 68.6
  percent.

## 5. Discussion

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**The offensive line rate is a selection, not a fact about linemen.** This
population requires a stat line, and linemen rarely appear in one. The 806
linemen in the risk set are those who recovered a fumble, caught a
deflection, or otherwise left a statistical trace, and their 8.2 percent
drafted rate describes that selected group. Models that use position should
treat the line as a thin-data category, not the position with the best
observed rate.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**Position is a feature the models should carry.** Both the level (a
sixfold spread in drafted rates) and the shape (round mix, average pick,
hazard timing, entry route) differ by position. A single pooled model would
spend its capacity explaining variance that position names in one column.
:::

Two caveats bound the figures. The not-recorded category holds 299 seasons,
under half a percent of the risk set, concentrated in earlier draft classes
whose roster entries lacked a usable position code, plus a few seasons with
no roster row at all; their rates are reported but not compared. And the
eligibility-clock imputation noted in the previous post applies here:
high-school graduation year is imputed for players without a recruiting
record, shifting rows in and out of the risk set. The shifts are not
position-specific, so the between-group comparisons are sturdier than the
absolute levels.
